Q1: Sodium dodecyl sulfate exhibits several known hazards, including significant acute and chronic environmental hazards, oral hazards, dermal and eye hazards, and organ/systemic hazards (all Tier 1). It also shows potential hazards for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity, and inhalation based on expanded scientific data (Tier 2), while information on its endocrine disruption potential is currently data deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: This chemical is not identified on any lists of concern. Instead, it is included on lists indicating low concern under specific conditions, such as the SCIL Green Circle list, which verifies low concern based on scientific data, and as a substance added to food, regulated by the FDA.
Q3: Sodium dodecyl sulfate is exceptionally well-characterized, evidenced by approximately 155,000 chemical literature references, significantly exceeding the median for similar materials. Its molecular formula is precisely defined, it is not classified as a poorly defined substance, and only one hazard class (endocrine disruption) is currently data deficient.
